summary: quorvex ships import-time Windows PE dropper disguised as empty placeholder
details: The package's main entry index.mjs contains a large base64-encoded Windows PE (MZ header) binary stored in a top-level PAYLOAD array. At module top level — reached on any require('quorvex') or import 'quorvex' — the module decodes the array via Buffer.from(PAYLOAD, 'base64') and writes the resulting ~355 KB executable to disk with writeFileSync(exePath, payloadBuffer). The README advertises the package as a placeholder with 'nothing in here yet', directly contradicting the shipped behavior. The dropped bytes are opaque, unrelated to any advertised functionality, and staged using only fs primitives — the shape of a stage-one dropper that materializes an attacker-controlled Windows executable onto the installer's filesystem the moment the module is loaded.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
